title: Secret set/list/inspect/delete
description: Spec §6.2 and §8. Hidden-input and --stdin exact-bytes entry; metadata-only inspection with no value, length, preview or hash; alias grammar; lookups scoped to the bound project only.

acceptanceCriteria.text: T08: hidden-input and stdin create/update, metadata read and explicit deletion work with no value/length/fingerprint disclosure
T09: sentinel values in rejected arguments, malformed input and synthetic exceptions never reach stdout/stderr
T11: a missing local alias neither falls back to another project nor enumerates its inventory

plan: 2. Domain: add a secrets collection to vault-state.ts (id, projectId, alias, value as strict base64 of opaque bytes, createdAt, updatedAt, revision), with the spec alias grammar and a 64 KiB value bound; an older document gains the collection without a version bump, following the existing localBindings precedent.

3. Application: src/application/secrets.ts with runSecret dispatching set/list/inspect/delete; hidden-input and stdin value entry behind an injected port; metadata-only results; replacement confirmation on the interactive path only; every lookup scoped to the checkout binding (absent or naming another project is refused, never a fallback).

4. Contract: new catalog codes (project_not_registered, secret_action_unknown, secret_alias_invalid, secret_requires_terminal, secret_stdin_terminal, secret_value_rejected, secret_value_too_large, secret_not_found) and the manifest entry for the secret command.

5. CLI: composition in main.ts (secretCommand and the dispatch branch), an adapter for hidden terminal entry, stdin bytes, and replacement confirmation; no value reaches argv, the environment, output or a prompt.

6. Tests: T08 (hidden and stdin create/replace, metadata list/inspect, delete, shape-pinned outputs with no value, length or hash), T09 (sentinel cases added to the rejected-argument and exception tables), T11 (two projects in one vault; a missing alias neither resolves elsewhere nor enumerates another project; an unregistered checkout is refused), alias grammar and value bounds, and contract-test harness provisioning for the new command.
7. Records and gates: task notes for the design points above; bun run check; lore check --strict; independent review over the diff; PR into dev with CI green; merge bare, then report.
finalSummary:
WCLI-8 delivers `ward secret set|list|inspect|delete` (spec §6.2, §8, §7.1), so a developer can put a credential into a project's vault without any value ever passing through an argument, an environment variable, a prompt, an output or an agent's context.

WHAT LANDED. The encrypted state document gains a `secrets` collection — opaque id, owning project, alias from the spec's grammar, opaque value bytes stored as canonical base64, timestamps, revision — gained without a version bump the way localBindings was, and carried through the two points that rebuild the document (registerCheckout and runRestore), each pinned by its own test because each was a place a careless edit would silently destroy stored records. Entry is hidden on a terminal (raw mode, no echo and no mask) or exact bytes through --stdin for trusted automation, which refuses a terminal as its source, where typing would be echoed. A value never reaches argv, the environment or any prompt, and every result is built from a fixed metadata field set that tests pin by key, so disclosure is excluded by construction rather than filtered. A replacement keeps the record's identity and revision and asks before overwriting on the interactive path; --stdin replaces without a prompt as the explicit non-interactive form. Every lookup is scoped to the checkout's binding and the decision is re-checked inside the write transaction; a miss stays a miss, and no other project's records are consulted, filtered in or counted. Eight new catalog codes carry the refusals, none echoing an alias or naming a value.

EVIDENCE. T08: hidden and stdin create and replace, list and inspect return metadata only, explicit delete, and no value, length or hash in any output. T09: sentinel rows added to the rejected-argument table (in process and packaged) plus an oversized value and a throwing source that never echo. T11: two projects in one vault; a missing alias neither falls back nor enumerates the other project; unregistered and mismatched checkouts are refused before any value is read. Independent review (opum-workflow:reviewer) over origin/dev..b5c5891 found one Medium and three Low findings plus two minors, and all six are addressed at 9ad8f10. The Medium was real: the hidden reader truncated at the bound instead of refusing, so an over-limit value would have stored a silent 64 KiB prefix while the catalog's too-large code stayed unreachable from the interactive path; a first attempt at the fix was itself caught by an end-to-end probe for swallowing the refusal into "empty or cancelled" before it landed, and both halves are now pinned by tests. The reviewer re-verified every fix at 9ad8f10, including real-pty probes (no echo, raw mode restored, prompts never on stdout, --stdin exact bytes with NUL and terminator, terminal refused as the stdin source) and independent isolation of each race test's mechanism. Mutations, predicted then measured: dropped project scope 3 of 31; dropped terminal gate 1 of 31; dropped size bound 2 of 31; removed transaction re-check 2 of 36 (0 of 32 before the fixes); removed confirmation precondition 1 of 36; restored truncating reader 2 of 36; swallowed refusal 1 of 36. Gates: bun run check exit 0, 425 tests 0 fail; lore validate --strict, lore check --strict, lore agents --check and the source-coverage check exit 0 with no docs concept touched. PR opum-ai/ward-cli#47; CI run 36513844170 green on 9ad8f10 (Check, Docs, Tracker integrity).

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. That a value is unreadable by the account that owns the vault: P0's boundary is guardrails inside a trusted account, stated in adr/0002 and unchanged here. Terminal state after an external kill mid-read, shared with the pre-existing passphrase path. The CLI's exit 5 for secret_changed is covered by the fixed error-type mapping table and the manifest declaration rather than asserted end to end, because the RunOptions seam has no store injection (recorded as a residual; the race itself is pinned at the application boundary). The stdin reader's buffer is not zeroed on refusal, the same best-effort posture the store documents. `ward instructions` and SKILL.md do not yet mention the secret commands: the guidance topics deliberately name no command as available, and the skill is WCLI-14's artifact.
